intended_object: A line bundle on a scheme Y rigidified along a morphism s : T → Y, meaning a pair (L, α) where L is an invertible 𝒪_Y-module and α : s^*L ≅ 𝒪_T is a trivialization of its pullback (Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models §8.1; Kleiman, The Picard scheme §9.2). This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The structure has two fields:
- `lineBundle : InvertibleSheaf Y`, an object of the full subcategory of `Y.Modules` whose objects are locally free of rank one.
- `rigidification`, an isomorphism of `𝒪_T`-modules from `(Scheme.Modules.pullback s).obj L` to `𝟙_ T.Modules`, the unit of the monoidal structure, which is the structure sheaf 𝒪_T.

This is exactly the data of a line bundle rigidified along s.

In the references, the rigidification is usually taken along a section ε : S → X or along a closed subscheme. Allowing an arbitrary morphism s : T → Y is the more general version and covers those cases.

Isomorphisms of rigidified bundles must be compatible with the trivializations. The library handles this correctly in the separate `setoid` definition.

The notion is standard for schemes. Mathlib has no notion of rigidified line bundles, and none of invertible sheaves on schemes either; the library defines `InvertibleSheaf` itself. So the definition is not stated more narrowly than an existing general notion.
